clue.text: Lisa died as a metaphysical entity

parts.note: Leonardo's portrait is the Mona Lisa, so Lisa calls up her first name Mona
d is the standard abbreviation for died in records and genealogies

explanation.surface: A woman called Lisa passed away as some kind of philosophical being.
explanation.walkthrough: Lisa leads to MONA through the famous painting, the Mona Lisa.
explanation.definitionFit: In Leibniz's philosophy a monad is the simple indivisible unit of being, a metaphysical substance.

clue.text: Sailor told to go away

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
someone told to go has been sent off

explanation.surface: A seaman is ordered off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not present, elsewhere, is said to be away from home or work.

clue.text: Maybe equipment a surfer takes to the coast

definitions.text: Maybe equipment a surfer takes to the coast

parts.words: Maybe equipment a surfer takes to the coast
parts.note: a surfer's kit is a board for riding the waves, so split the answer as the water plus a plank; the whole thing means the shoreline

explanation.surface: A surfer carries gear down to the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: The land along the edge of the ocean is the coastline region of a country.

clue.text: Herb adds unfermented beer to drinking vessel

indicators.note: adds ... to puts the beer word after the vessel word, joining them in that order

parts.note: a mug is a large cup for drinks
wort is the malt infusion before it ferments into beer

explanation.surface: A brewer tips some unfinished beer into a tankard.
explanation.definitionFit: Mugwort is a wayside plant of the artemisia family, used in herbal remedies and once to flavour ale.

clue.text: Legitimate target the umpire is there to see

definitions.meaning: something open to attack or criticism by fair rules

definitions.text: the umpire is there to see
definitions.meaning: an umpire ensures a contest is played fairly, by the rules

explanation.surface: An official watches over a target that may lawfully be hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A legitimate object of ridicule or pursuit; and a match played honestly is what an umpire oversees.

clue.text: Anything but all dressed up with nowhere to go!

definitions.meaning: wearing no clothes at all, naked
having no engagements arranged, a free diary

explanation.surface: A play on the saying about being all dressed up with nowhere to go.
explanation.definitionFit: Naked means wearing no garments; and an empty social calendar means no events planned.

clue.text: Ran to the top, apparently in great pain

parts.note: to double is to run at a quick pace, as soldiers doubling
up means towards the top

explanation.surface: Someone sprinted to the summit, it seems, and was in agony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' tells you the surface reading of the phrase is literal: ran upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent over with a stomach cramp or laughter, someone is folded forward in agony.

clue.text: The rasher of 13th century scientists

definitions.meaning: a slice of cured pork for frying, and also read as more rash
Roger ... was an English friar and experimental scientist of the 1200s

explanation.surface: Which medieval scientist was the most reckless?
explanation.definitionFit: Cured pork is sold in slices called rashers; and Roger Bacon was a pioneering medieval scholar.

clue.text: Southern county known in northern areas

definitions.meaning: A county in south-east England
in Scots and northern dialect, ken means know, so the past participle is known

explanation.surface: A southern county is recognised in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Kent lies in south-east England; and in Scottish dialect it is the past form of ken, to know.

clue.text: Invitation to perform on violin and acknowledge the applause

definitions.meaning: a violinist picks up the bow to start playing
a performer bends forward to thank the audience

explanation.surface: A violinist is invited to play and then thanks the clapping audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A request to pick up the fiddlestick, and a performer's customary gesture of thanks at the end.

clue.text: Robust and hearty disposition

indicators.note: disposition read as arrangement, so the letters of hearty are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A person described as sturdy with a warm-hearted character.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is down-to-earth and lusty, a coarse vigorous quality.

clue.text: Mediterranean mount which returns one's stake

indicators.note: returns asks for the stake word to come back, read from right to left

parts.note: the ante is the stake put up in poker before the deal

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean peak where a gambler gets his money back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns ANTE to give the volcano in Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano in Sicily, an island mountain in that sea.

clue.text: How a redundant worker tries to get back on the rails?

definitions.text: How a redundant worker tries to get back on the rails?

parts.words: How a redundant worker tries to get back on the rails?
parts.note: a laid-off worker learns new skills; read the word as ..., putting carriages back on the tracks

explanation.surface: A sacked employee tries to get his life back on track.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone made redundant takes fresh instruction for another job, to rebuild a career.

clue.text: How knitters set out to begin an argument

definitions.meaning: knitting begins by casting on the first line of stitches
a row, rhyming with cow, is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Knitting circle members start a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses depend on two pronunciations of the same spelling: a line of stitches and a noisy dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitters work line by line of stitches; and to provoke a quarrel is the second sense.

clue.text: Turns up and listens

definitions.meaning: to be present at an event
to pay attention to what is said, as attend to

explanation.surface: Someone arrives and pays attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To be present at a meeting; and to heed or pay attention.

clue.text: All the Walrus and the Carpenter managed to eat

definitions.meaning: every person, the whole lot

definitions.text: the Walrus and the Carpenter managed to eat
definitions.meaning: in Lewis Carroll's poem the pair ate all the oysters, leaving not a single one

explanation.surface: A nod to Lewis Carroll's greedy pair who gobble up the oysters.
explanation.definitionFit: Each and every person, the whole company; and in the poem not a single oyster was left uneaten.

clue.text: Enamoured of pudding now being served

parts.note: a pudding is a dessert, a sweet course
a dish that is on is on the menu or in progress

explanation.surface: A diner is in love with the dessert that has just arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: To be infatuated with someone is to be taken with them, fond.

clue.text: The trek has ended in total victory

parts.note: a trek is a long walk
something finished is over

explanation.surface: A hike is finished, and it was a triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy win in which the opponent offers no contest, an unopposed victory.

clue.text: Use a bike to go about on like the wind

indicators.note: go about means to surround, so the bike word is placed around the other piece

parts.note: to cycle is to ride a bicycle

explanation.surface: A cyclist rides off as fast as a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclone is a violent rotating storm, a fierce gale.

clue.text: Allowance made for priceless fringe stage production

parts.note: something without a price is free of charge
a fringe show is a play staged away from the main theatres

explanation.surface: A grant is given for a free show at an alternative theatre festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway or latitude given to something is room to move, slack.

clue.text: 10 distributed before Easter

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as '10 distributed before Easter' (4): 10 is TAKE A BOW, which gives nothing towards LENT, and 'distributed' does not mean lent; the cross-reference or a word is misread and no scan is available

clue.text: Behold, morning reveals the rich earth

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look, behold
am, ante meridiem, is the morning

explanation.surface: Look, dawn breaks over fertile soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Loam is fertile soil of clay, sand and humus, good for growing.

clue.text: A horse staggered to the beach

indicators.note: a staggering creature lurches about, so the letters of a horse are jumbled

explanation.surface: A horse lurches down to the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Onto land from the water, on the beach is where a landing party goes.

clue.text: Wide, but not wide enough to T be a main highway apparently

definitions.meaning: of great width

definitions.text: not wide enough to T be a main highway apparently
definitions.meaning: British roads are graded A for main routes and B for lesser ones

explanation.surface: Something wide that still falls short of a major highway.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain main roads are A roads and minor ones B roads; split the answer as B ROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Of great width from side to side; and a secondary British road graded B.

clue.text: Great gorge could be seen over there

parts.note: can means is able to, could
yon is an old word for yonder, over there

explanation.surface: A huge ravine is visible in the distance.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep steep-sided valley cut by a river, like the one in Arizona.

clue.text: I say! Take a gander

definitions.meaning: an exclamation to get someone's attention
gander is slang for a look, so this means have a look at this spot

explanation.surface: An exclamation inviting someone to have a look.
explanation.definitionFit: A call for attention, as in 'now listen'; and an invitation to glance at something nearby.

clue.text: Spherical bullet

definitions.meaning: shaped like a ball
a single shot or cartridge for a gun

explanation.surface: A ball-shaped piece of ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ball-shaped, circular; and a single cartridge of ammunition is counted as one shot.

clue.text: Running away like a priest on his sabbatical?

definitions.meaning: fleeing, falling back from an enemy

definitions.text: like a priest on his sabbatical?
definitions.meaning: a priest may go away for a period of prayer and seclusion

explanation.surface: A priest on leave seems to be fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: An army falling back is withdrawing; and a cleric on a spiritual break is away in seclusion.
